newsitem.title: USA: US House's Leach offers compromise banking bill.
newsitem.headline: US House's Leach offers compromise banking bill.

text.p: The chairman of the House Banking Committee proposed compromise legislation Monday to shore up the thrift industry insurance fund, cut regulatory red tape for banks and modernize the banking system.
Rep. Jim Leach, an Iowa Republican, said he believes the measure will win support from key banking and industry groups. Leach pulled the plug on an earlier version after it ran into stiff opposition.
Leach said he believes "we are now at a point" where his proposal will have the support of major banking and insurance groups.
He said he plans to ask House leaders to schedule action on the legislation "at the earliest possible time."

Leach said the new proposal -- drafted after extensive talks with House Democrats -- includes legislation approved by his committee earlier this year to shore up the Savings Association Insurance Fund.
It also includes "noncontroversial" elements of earlier legislation aimed at modernizing the banking industry.
The proposal excludes earlier controversial language covering the Community Reinvestment Act and banks' involvement in insurance activities.
And to meet objections voiced by Democrats, it scales back earlier proposals to cut regulatory red tape for banks.
Among particular items, the proposal calls for a General Accounting Office study of state supervision of national bank insurance activities.

In addition, the "closely related to banking" test under the Bank Holding Company Act would be changed to a "financial in nature or incidental to such financial activities" test, with an amendment clarifying that "financial in nature" does not mean insurance or annuities.
